sample_unit: messages (1,800 simulated plus 794 Aegis mental health-related)

links.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of safety filter detecting mental health crises in messages (missed vs unnecessary flags)
links.effect: On the Verily dataset, sensitivity was 0.990 and specificity 0.992 for any crisis; on Aegis, sensitivity was 0.982 and specificity 0.859.
links.quote: The VBHSF demonstrated, well-balanced performance on the Verily Mental Health Crisis Dataset v1.0, achieving high sensitivity (0.990) and specificity (0.992) in detecting any mental health crises.

links.outcome: Sensitivity of general content moderation guardrails for specific mental health crisis types
links.effect: NeMo and OpenAI Omni Moderation showed inconsistent performance across crisis types, with sensitivity below 0.10 for some categories, meaning missed crises.
links.quote: NVIDIA NeMo and OpenAI Omni Moderation Latest exhibited inconsistent performance across specific crisis types, with sensitivity for some categories falling below 0.10.

unlisted_practices: Deploying a dedicated behavioral health safety filter in front of LLM conversations to detect mental health crises

screen.practice: crisis-detection safety filter for LLM conversations
screen.reason: The study empirically benchmarks and compares specific AI safety filters/guardrails (Verily behavioral health safety filter vs OpenAI Omni Moderation and NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails) designed to catch mental health crises in text conversations.

primary.practice: safety filters and content moderation guardrails
